data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical antibacterials & antiseptics_

**Class:** Triphenylmethane (aniline) dye; antiseptic

## Mechanism of action
- Binds microbial DNA and disrupts cell walls → active against Gram-positive bacteria (including MRSA) and Candida; also anti-angiogenic

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Intertrigo, candidiasis (oral thrush — 0.5%), weeping eczema, chronic paronychia, MRSA colonised wounds, tinea pedis maceration

## Dose & formulations
- Paint once or twice daily for a few days (0.5–1% aqueous)

## Adverse effects
- Purple staining of skin and clothes; irritation, ulceration on mucosa with strong solutions; contact dermatitis
- Tattooing if applied to granulation tissue; possible carcinogenicity in animals (restricted in some countries)

## Contraindications
- Ulcerated or granulating areas; mucosa with high concentrations

## Pregnancy & lactation
Small areas acceptable.

## Viva points
- Antiseptic dye — Gram-positive and Candida; stains purple

_Sources: Khopkar ch.30 (Eusol/Gentian violet). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
